title: Allah is good
hookLine: Allah is good and accepts only the good, and the traveler's du'a is blocked by unlawful food
tomorrow: one short line for every gray area. what is it?

lines: SORT BY: WHERE IT CAME FROM.
cards: Every shopping app lets you sort: cheapest, fastest, best rated. None of them lets you sort by where the money in your account came from. Yesterday's question asked about a traveler whose prayer isn't answered.
Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, describing him. A long journey. Hair wild, covered in dust, hands stretched up to the sky.
O Lord, O Lord. Everything about him looks sincere. Then the hadith adds one more detail.

teach.b: His food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothes are unlawful, and he's been nourished on the unlawful. So how can he be answered? The hadith opens with the principle.

teach.h: ALLAH IS GOOD, ACCEPTS THE GOOD.
teach.b: Allah is good, tayyib, and accepts only what is good. The same command went to the messengers and to the believers. In Pickthall's words: "O ye messengers! Eat of the good things, and do right."
Now the question at the end, and two ways of hearing it.
The first hears a wall. A prayer fed on the unlawful doesn't rise, so clean up the income before raising your hands.

teach.h: READING TWO: FAR OFF, NOT SHUT.
teach.b: Its best case: the hadith stacks up every sign of a prayer that should be answered, the journey, the dust, the raised hands, the Lord's name twice, and still asks how.
The second, which commentators such as Ibn Rajab give, hears the question as making the answer far off, not impossible.

Allah still answers whom He wills, and the door of repentance stays open. Its best case: the hadith asks a question; it doesn't announce a sentence. Both readings agree on the part that touches an ordinary Tuesday.
One to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, the receipt is part of the du'a.

how: Muslims take care that their earnings and food are halal; someone who finds unlawful money in their hands is taught to return it to its owner where possible, and to repent.

o: Allah answers anyone who prays sincerely
Allah is good and accepts only what is good
Allah forgives whatever people happen to do

games.q: the good, and the traveler — tap the pairs.
p: dusty, hands raised, fed on the unlawful
eat of the good things, and do right
a wall, or far off: two readings

s: a sincere enough prayer is answered no matter what you live on
the traveler shows every sign of sincerity, and the hadith still asks: how can he be answered?
the command to eat good things went to the messengers and the believers alike
the hadith says Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers.

games.q: you've always heard: 'if your money's unclean, Allah won't hear you, period.' state the other reading at its strongest.
o: the hadith asks a question; it makes the answer far off, but doesn't shut the door.
the hadith is only about travelers, so it doesn't apply to people at home.
the hadith is about food only; money has nothing to do with prayer.
games.why: commentators such as Ibn Rajab read 'how can he be answered?' as making it far off, not impossible. both readings agree: what you earn is part of your prayer.

practice: Take out one coin, a bill or a card, or open your banking app to a single line. Look at it for the sit as if it could tell you its story: where did it come from, and is that a place you'd be glad to name in a prayer?
If something seems off, you don't have to fix it in two minutes; let yourself see it clearly.

wordCard.voice: Allah is good: tayyib, good and pure, and accepting only what is good. What you eat and earn travels with what you ask.

orig.note: Arabic: Allah is good. tayyib means good and pure.

carryVoice: The line for today: clean food, open door, because what you earn travels with what you ask. Day twelve, done.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 1015 (Abu Hurayrah: Allah is good and accepts only the good; the dusty traveler; 'how can he be answered?')

sources.q: O ye messengers! Eat of the good things, and do right.

sources.ref: Qur'an 2:172 (O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you)
Ibn Rajab, Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam, on hadith 10 ('how can he be answered' as making it unlikely, not impossible)
